deck.title: Incident Investigation and Corrective Action Concept Cards

cards.backDefinition: A structured examination of a work-related incident or close call to determine what happened, why it happened, and what must change to prevent recurrence.
cards.whyItMatters: A disciplined investigation can expose hazards and program weaknesses that would remain hidden if the organization only records the outcome or assigns blame.
cards.keyPoint: The purpose is prevention through learning and corrective action, not fault finding.

sourceRefs.locator: Investigating a Worksite Incident
Purpose of the Guide - Why Investigate?

cards.backDefinition: A work-related incident that could have caused serious injury or illness but did not, often because circumstances were only slightly different.
cards.whyItMatters: Close calls reveal hazards and system weaknesses without the human cost of an injury, giving the organization an opportunity to learn before a more serious event occurs.
cards.keyPoint: Investigate close calls with the same prevention mindset used for harmful incidents.

sourceRefs.locator: Principles of Incident Investigations > key terms > Close Call
Overview > close calls or near misses

cards.backDefinition: An investigation approach that looks beyond the worker action nearest the event to underlying program, design, planning, organizational, technical, and operational factors.
cards.whyItMatters: Stopping at a behavior or immediate condition can leave the system weakness intact, allowing similar incidents to recur under the same underlying conditions.
cards.keyPoint: Ask what in the system created or allowed the conditions for the event.

sourceRefs.locator: Principles of Incident Investigations > Investigate Programs, Not Behaviors
Investigating a Worksite Incident > look beyond immediate causes

cards.backDefinition: Protecting and documenting relevant physical conditions at an incident scene before evidence is moved, altered, lost, or contaminated.
cards.whyItMatters: Preserving the scene protects the factual basis of the investigation and helps the team reconstruct conditions and event sequences more reliably.
cards.keyPoint: Emergency response and life safety come first; preserve what remains once the scene is safe to investigate.

sourceRefs.locator: Four-Step Systems Approach > Step 1 Preserve/Document the Scene

cards.backDefinition: Systematic collection of observations, interviews, records, logs, photographs, documents, and other information needed to reconstruct the event and its conditions.
cards.whyItMatters: A broad evidence base reduces premature conclusions and helps investigators compare accounts, establish sequence, and identify contributing system factors.
cards.keyPoint: Collect information from multiple sources before settling on a causal explanation.

sourceRefs.locator: Four-Step Systems Approach > Step 2 Collect Information
Root Cause Analysis Tools > interviews and review of documents

cards.backDefinition: A direct or readily visible condition or action associated with an incident that may explain the event locally without explaining the underlying system failure.
cards.whyItMatters: Correcting only the immediate cause can remove a symptom while leaving the conditions that allowed the problem to develop and recur.
cards.keyPoint: Immediate cause answers what was closest to the event; root cause asks why the system allowed it.

sourceRefs.locator: Root cause analysis > underlying or systemic rather than generalized or immediate causes
Investigating a Worksite Incident > look beyond immediate causes

cards.backDefinition: A fundamental, underlying, system-related reason an incident occurred that identifies one or more correctable failures in the way work is designed or managed.
cards.whyItMatters: Root causes point toward system changes that can prevent recurrence instead of merely treating the visible symptom of an incident.
cards.keyPoint: An incident may have more than one root cause.

sourceRefs.locator: Root cause definition and How to Conduct a Root Cause Analysis
Principles of Incident Investigations > Root Causes

cards.backDefinition: A structured analysis that asks what, how, and why an incident occurred to identify the underlying systemic causes and correctable failures behind the event.
cards.whyItMatters: Root cause analysis connects incident evidence to prevention by identifying the deeper conditions that must change for recurrence risk to be reduced.
cards.keyPoint: Use enough depth and more than one line of inquiry when the event is complex.

sourceRefs.locator: How to Conduct a Root Cause Analysis and Root Cause Analysis Tools
Investigating a Worksite Incident > underlying or root causes

cards.backDefinition: An event, condition, decision, action, or system weakness that contributed to how an incident developed and helps explain the pathway from conditions to outcome.
cards.whyItMatters: Identifying multiple causal factors prevents the investigation from collapsing a complex event into one convenient explanation and supports deeper root-cause analysis.
cards.keyPoint: A causal factor can contribute to the event without being the deepest root cause.

sourceRefs.locator: Root Cause Analysis Tools > Causal Factor Determination
Investigating a Worksite Incident > discover and correct all factors contributing to an incident

cards.backDefinition: A chronological reconstruction of relevant events, actions, conditions, and changes before, during, and after an incident to support causal analysis.
cards.whyItMatters: A timeline makes sequence and timing visible, helping investigators find gaps, interactions, conflicting evidence, and points where controls failed or could have intervened.
cards.keyPoint: Use the timeline to organize evidence, not as a substitute for root-cause reasoning.

sourceRefs.locator: Root Cause Analysis Tools > Timelines
Collect Information and determine event sequence

cards.backDefinition: An action taken to address an identified cause, hazard, or program deficiency so the same or a similar incident is less likely to occur again.
cards.whyItMatters: An investigation has little preventive value unless findings are translated into effective changes that control the conditions and system failures revealed by the evidence.
cards.keyPoint: Correct the underlying causes, not only the visible consequence of the event.

sourceRefs.locator: Four-Step Systems Approach > Step 4 Implement Corrective Actions
Investigating a Worksite Incident > identify and implement corrective actions

cards.backDefinition: Follow-up evaluation that confirms a corrective action was implemented and is effectively controlling the identified problem or preventing recurrence.
cards.whyItMatters: Administrative closure does not prove risk reduction; effectiveness verification checks whether the change works in practice and whether additional improvement is needed.
cards.keyPoint: Verify both implementation and continuing effectiveness.

sourceRefs.locator: Verify key processes and actions are preventing recurrence
Communicate investigation results and prioritize corrective actions
